correctness.rationale: For each edge split A|B, expected inclusion is length times (1-P(no survivors in A))(1-P(no survivors in B)). The four protection cases give +length Q on a pair-separating edge and length(Q-Q/Q_away) otherwise. The sum equals Q(L - sum_off length/Q_away). Every away-side extinction product is strictly increasing along the assumed risk trajectory; at least one exists whenever a third taxon is present; their reciprocals diverge near zero and tend to 1 near one. The intermediate value theorem proves exactly one sign-changing root. The n=2 exceptional case has positive H throughout. Recomputed exact three-leaf values -1/64, 0, 1/8 and independently compared all 120 edge expectations, 39 pair identities, and 369 anchored inequalities in two small trees. No finite test is substituted for the universal argument.

originality.rationale: The strongest inspected theorem (Steel–Mimoto–Mooers 2007, Theorem 3.2) gives the exact first-order unrooted HED contribution for arbitrary independent risks, from which the fixed-risk second difference can be derived. The presently assessed statement is the global one-crossing law: for each taxon pair on each tree with at least three taxa, every continuous strictly coordinatewise increasing family of risks from zero to one has exactly one change from negative to positive joint-protection interaction. That new quantified monotone-risk threshold and its genuine two-taxon boundary are neither asserted nor directly evaluated in inspected Theorem 3.2/4.1, and the proof supplies the missing sign and endpoint argument. The result is structurally distinct from rooted deterministic-anchor submodularity and from individual optimal species ranking changes. A substantial prior-implication risk from the close HED identity and an uninspected complementary-set article is disclosed.

value.rationale: Joint conservation choice is not necessarily captured by ranking taxa one at a time. The new qualitative theorem guarantees for every pair on every eligible unrooted tree that heterogeneously increasing extinction severity induces exactly one switch from redundancy to synergy; it rules out multiple reversals without any common risk formula. It also explains the sharp distinction from already anchored, submodular optimization. This is a motivated structural boundary of the expected diversity objective, not a numeric perturbation or arbitrary slice; its limitations are independent extinction and guaranteed survival.
